head: 33ad6f7561f67e71bfd8c4c10ae6e2df7e750701
summary:
The only content change since f9c303e is eng/rules-harness/plants.json, and the fix is real. The nine SL-089 rows (F36–F40, P28–P31) used to anchor on a cut-off piece of a line. The harness places a row only where the anchor equals a whole stripped line (harness.py:358-362), so none of the nine was ever planted or judged. That defect was already in the code on my first lap and I passed it.

Each row now anchors on the full text of WindowReport.cs:276, and I confirmed that text matches exactly one line of the file.

I ran the harness myself (`harness.py --only F36,F38,F40,P28,P30,P31` with the engine's interpreter): exit 0, clean baseline, all 6 rows AS-RECORDED. F36 (the two-line fluent layout), F38 and F40 fire in both xUnit and Fitness; P28, P30 and P31 stay quiet in both. 0 stray hits, and the scratch copy was removed afterwards.

The diff left one statement stale. The `_note` in plants.json still says 'F36-F40 and P28-P31 are expectations written at SL-089's build, which no harness run has recorded yet'. That is now false: this build's run recorded them (102/102 AS-RECORDED by the builder's account, which my 6-row run confirms). I put it in drift rather than as a finding, because the wording has no runtime effect.

O-036 (the census's other quoting spellings) is waived to SC-135, so not building it matches its disposition. Nothing in the tree contradicts the design beyond what earlier rounds recorded.

Second round: Nothing new in this second pass. The diff is the nine anchor strings in eng/rules-harness/plants.json, and I tried to break them as follows.

- **Line format.** The harness compares `plain(line).strip()` to the stripped anchor (harness.py:358-362). That makes CRLF, trailing whitespace and indentation in WindowReport.cs harmless. The anchor line carries no comment for `plain()` to remove.
- **Uniqueness.** The full anchor text matches exactly one line of WindowReport.cs (line 276). There is no second block the harness could plant into first.
- **Several rows on one anchor.** All nine rows share the anchor and are planted in one batch, in order. I checked whether the must-fire rows could make a must-stay-quiet row fire, or land hits on its line. The pattern only looks forward from the token on its own line, so the neighbouring planted lines cannot turn P28–P31 into hits. My harness run planted F36, F38, F40, P28, P30 and P31 together: all were AS-RECORDED, with 0 stray hits.
- **Partial failure.** If line 276 ever changes, the rows come back PLANT-BROKEN, which the harness reports loudly. They no longer pass silently as unjudged.

The stale `_note` sentence remains recorded in round 1's drift.

drift: eng/rules-harness/plants.json `_note` still ends 'F36-F40 and P28-P31 are expectations written at SL-089's build, which no harness run has recorded yet.' This build's harness run recorded them (builder: 102 rows, 102 AS-RECORDED, exit 0; my run of 6 of them agreed). The note's convention for other slices (e.g. SL-095's 'recorded by SL-095's build run of the harness (--only S14-S26: 13 AS-RECORDED, exit 0 ...)') is to name the run, so the sentence should say SL-089's build run recorded them.
